meta.title: Eligibility Health Check
meta.description: A self-audit for behavioral health organizations: pinpoint eligibility gaps and what to fix first.

intro.headline: Eligibility Health Check
intro.subheadline: A Self-Audit for Behavioral Health Organizations
intro.body: Most eligibility problems show up as a slow, steady bleed: denied claims, rework, and revenue you didn't know you were losing. This 2-minute assessment will help you pinpoint where your gaps are and what to fix first.

questions.text: Who owns insurance verification at intake?

options.label: A designated role with clear accountability
It's generally handled by intake staff, but ownership varies
It depends on the day — whoever is available

questions.text: Are patient demographics validated against payer records before the first visit?

options.label: Yes — we verify against the payer before the first appointment
Sometimes, but it's not a required step in our workflow
No — we enter what the patient reports and correct later if needed

questions.text: Do you capture secondary and tertiary coverage at intake?

options.label: Yes — we collect and document all known coverage
We ask, but it's not consistently captured
We typically only collect primary coverage

questions.text: How far in advance do you run eligibility checks before appointments?

options.label: 3–5 days out, with time to act on exceptions
The night before or morning of
We don't run them consistently before visits

questions.text: When a batch check returns an inactive result, what happens next?

options.label: There's a defined escalation path and a clear owner
Someone follows up, but the process isn't formalized
It often falls through the cracks until the claim denies

questions.text: Are you reviewing benefit details (plan type, copay, deductible) — or just confirming active coverage?

options.label: We review full benefit details and document them
We glance at details but mainly check active/inactive
We only check whether coverage is active

questions.text: Can your staff run real-time eligibility checks at the point of care?

options.label: Yes — and they're trained on when to use it
The capability exists, but it's rarely used
No — we rely entirely on batch checks

questions.text: What happens when a patient arrives and their coverage status has changed since the batch check?

options.label: We have a documented protocol for handling discrepancies
Staff figure it out case by case
We usually find out after the claim denies

questions.text: Do you have a differentiated process for payers or programs with higher coverage volatility?

options.label: Yes — we treat high-volatility payers differently
We're aware of which payers are volatile, but the process is the same
No — all payers go through the same process

questions.text: When you get an eligibility-related denial, what's the first step?

options.label: Investigate root cause before resubmitting
It depends on the staff member handling it
Resubmit and hope for a different result

questions.text: Do you use insurance discovery tools to find coverage the patient didn't report?

options.label: Yes — it's part of our standard denial workflow
We have access but don't use them consistently
No — we don't have discovery tools in place

questions.text: Are eligibility denials tracked by root cause, or just by denial code?

options.label: By root cause — we categorize and trend them
We track denial codes but don't dig into root cause
We don't have a structured way to track them

questions.text: How often do you audit patient demographics for accuracy?

options.label: On a regular schedule — quarterly or more frequently
Occasionally, usually when a problem surfaces
We don't have a demographic audit process

questions.text: When a claim is rejected for a demographic mismatch, where does the correction happen?

options.label: In the patient record — we fix the source
On the claim itself, but not always in the patient record
Wherever is fastest — there's no standard

questions.text: Do you have a process for identifying and merging duplicate patient records?

options.label: Yes — with regular reviews and a defined merge process
We address duplicates when we stumble across them
We know we have duplicates but haven't tackled it

questions.text: Is there a clearly designated owner for eligibility performance?

options.label: Yes — a named person or role with defined accountability
Responsibility is shared but no single owner
Ownership is unclear — it's spread across teams

questions.text: Are eligibility workflows documented well enough to survive staff turnover?

options.label: Yes — fully documented and regularly updated
Partially — some documentation exists
No — most of it lives in people's heads

questions.text: Do you have a dashboard showing eligibility denial rates by payer, program, or location?

options.label: Yes — and we review it regularly
We have some reporting, but it's not centralized or routine
No — we don't have eligibility-specific reporting

questions.text: Do you know your current cost per eligibility denial (staff time, rework, write-offs)?

options.label: Yes — we've quantified it
We have a rough sense but haven't calculated it
No — we haven't measured it

questions.text: Can you see how many upcoming appointments have unverified eligibility?

options.label: Yes — we have real-time visibility into upcoming appointment eligibility status
We can pull it, but it requires manual effort
No — we don't have that view

tiers.label: Strong Foundation
tiers.summary: Your eligibility processes are well-built. Focus on the sections below to close remaining gaps.

tiers.label: Room to Improve
tiers.summary: You have some good practices in place, but inconsistencies are likely costing you. The sections below show where.

tiers.label: Significant Gaps
tiers.summary: Your eligibility process has meaningful gaps that are very likely contributing to preventable denials and lost revenue.

sectionTiers.label: Solid
sectionTiers.body: This area looks solid. Keep it up.

sectionTiers.label: Some Gaps
sectionTiers.body: Some gaps here — worth tightening up.

sectionTiers.label: Priority
sectionTiers.body: This is a priority area. It's likely contributing to preventable revenue loss.

insights.label: Gaps everywhere
insights.body: Your gaps are spread across multiple areas — and you're not alone. Many behavioral health organizations are running eligibility processes built for a simpler coverage environment. A co-sourced RCM partner can help close these gaps systematically.

insights.label: Upstream data quality
insights.body: Your biggest opportunity is upstream data quality. The fixes here are process and training-oriented — and they're some of the fastest to implement.

insights.label: Workflow timing
insights.body: Your gap is in workflow. You likely have the right information but aren't acting on it at the right time. The right tools can close this quickly.

insights.label: Visibility & recovery
insights.body: Your issue is visibility and recovery. Revenue is leaking and you may not have full line of sight into how much. Discovery tools and denial analytics are the highest-leverage investment here.

insights.label: Weakest section
insights.body: Your most significant gap is in **{{weakestSection}}**. Strengthening this area will have the most immediate impact on your eligibility performance.
